lessons.title: What is GWDB?
lessons.summary: Understand the purpose of GWDB and how subject tables organise groundwater information.
objectives: Recognise Registration as the mandatory facility record.
Identify examples of GWDB subject tables.
lessons.contentMarkdown:
# What is GWDB?

The Groundwater Database, or **GWDB**, stores information about groundwater facilities and related scientific, operational and administrative records.

GWDB is a relational database. Information is separated into subject tables such as Registration, Casing, Aquifer, Water Level and Water Analysis.

## Central idea

A record must exist in the Registration table before information can be stored in another GWDB subject table.

## Remember

- GWDB contains multiple related tables.
- Registration identifies the facility.
- Registered Number connects records belonging to that facility.

lessons.title: Database Fundamentals
lessons.summary: Learn tables, fields, rows, keys and relationships using GWDB examples.
lessons.contentMarkdown:
# Database Fundamentals

A **table** contains rows with the same field structure. A **field** stores one item of information. A **row** combines fields into one record.

For example, a Strata Log row contains Registered Number, Record, Top of Strata, Bottom of Strata and Description.

GWDB commonly identifies records using Registered Number, Pipe, Date and Record.

lessons.title: Registered Number (RN)
lessons.summary: Learn how RN uniquely identifies a facility and connects records across GWDB tables.
lessons.contentMarkdown:
# Registered Number (RN)

The **Registered Number**, commonly called the **RN**, is the most important identifier in the Groundwater Database.

## 1. What is an RN?

Every facility in GWDB is assigned a Registered Number. A facility could be a production bore, monitoring bore, test bore, proposed bore, surface-water facility or another facility for which information must be recorded.

Example: `Registered Number: 123456`

The RN's purpose is to uniquely identify the facility.

## 2. Where is the RN created?

The facility's main record is stored in the **Registration table**. The data dictionary states that a Registration record must exist before information can be stored in another GWDB subject table.

| Registered Number | Facility Type | Status | Office |
|---|---|---|---|
| 123456 | Sub-artesian Facility | Existing | Brisbane |

## 3. How does RN connect the tables?

The same RN is recorded in subject tables containing information about the facility.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    R[Registration - RN 123456]
    C[Casing - RN 123456]
    S[Strata Log - RN 123456]
    A[Aquifer - RN 123456]
    W[Water Level - RN 123456]
    Q[Water Analysis - RN 123456]
    I[Images - RN 123456]
    R --> C
    R --> S
    R --> A
    R --> W
    R --> Q
    R --> I
```

This allows GWDB to assemble the facility's construction, geology, monitoring, water-quality and document history.

## 4. RN is a business key

RN identifies a real facility and is understood by groundwater staff. It is therefore a **business key**. This differs from a technical identifier such as a generated UUID that may only have meaning inside an application.

In the existing GWDB, RN is the central business identifier. The physical Oracle datatype and constraints must be verified from database metadata.

## 5. Is RN enough to identify every row?

No. RN identifies the facility, but a facility can have many related records.

| RN | Pipe | Date | Measurement |
|---|---|---|---:|
| 123456 | A | 01/08/2026 | -14.3 m |
| 123456 | A | 02/08/2026 | -14.5 m |
| 123456 | A | 03/08/2026 | -14.4 m |

All three measurements belong to the same facility. A particular Water Level row may require a combination such as `RN + Pipe + Date + Time`. Therefore RN identifies the facility while additional fields identify a child record.

## 6. RN creates one-to-many relationships

One Registration row can be associated with many Casing, Aquifer, Water Level, Water Analysis and Image rows.

| Parent | Child | Logical cardinality |
|---|---|---|
| Registration | Casing | One-to-many |
| Registration | Aquifer | One-to-many |
| Registration | Water Level | One-to-many |
| Registration | Water Analysis | One-to-many |
| Registration | Images | One-to-many |

The logical relationship is documented through RN usage. Whether Oracle enforces each relationship with a physical foreign-key constraint remains to be verified.

## 7. RN and multiple pipes

One registered facility can have multiple pipes.

| Registered Number | Pipe |
|---|---|
| 123456 | A |
| 123456 | B |
| 123456 | C |

The RN identifies the facility, while Pipe distinguishes an individual pipe within it. Pipe `A` represents a single pipe or the deepest pipe; later letters identify additional pipes according to the documented depth convention.

## 8. RN of a bore replaced

Registration contains the field **RN of Bore Replaced**. This allows a new facility record to refer to the bore it replaced.

| New RN | RN of Bore Replaced |
|---|---|
| 234567 | 123456 |

This is logically a self-referencing relationship from Registration back to Registration. The physical Oracle constraint must be verified.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    NEW[Replacement bore - RN 234567]
    OLD[Old bore - RN 123456]
    NEW -->|RN of Bore Replaced| OLD
```

## 9. Investigation-bore numbering convention

The data dictionary states that eight- and nine-digit numbers may be allocated to departmental investigation bores. For these numbers, the first four digits represent the surface-water drainage basin and sub-basin.

This means some RNs may contain historical or geographic meaning. Do not assume that every RN follows the same format until production data has been profiled.

## 10. RN data-quality and schema checks

When Oracle access is available, verify:

- RN uniqueness in Registration.
- The Oracle datatype, length and formatting of RN.
- Whether leading zeros are possible or significant.
- Minimum and maximum RN lengths and values.
- Duplicate Registration records.
- Subject-table RNs missing from Registration.
- Physical foreign-key constraints.
- Validity of RN of Bore Replaced values.
- Whether RNs can be changed, reused or retired.
- How RNs are generated, allocated or reserved.
- Whether sequences, Forms routines or PL/SQL allocate RNs.

## 11. Documented versus inferred

| Statement | Evidence status |
|---|---|
| Every facility is assigned an RN | Documented |
| RN uniquely identifies a facility | Documented |
| RN is common to GWDB tables | Documented |
| Registration must exist before other subject data | Documented |
| Registration to Water Level is logically one-to-many | Inferred from documented structure |
| Oracle contains a physical foreign key for the relationship | Not yet verified |
| RN is generated using an Oracle sequence | Unknown |

A logical relationship may exist even when the database does not enforce it through a physical foreign-key constraint.

## Lesson summary

1. RN uniquely identifies a GWDB facility.
2. Registration is the facility's central record.
3. The same RN connects related subject-table records.
4. RN identifies the facility but does not uniquely identify every child row.
5. Pipe, Date and Record help identify individual related records.
6. Replacement bores can logically reference an earlier RN.
7. Oracle metadata is required to confirm physical keys and constraints.
keyTakeaways: RN uniquely identifies a GWDB facility.
Registration is the facility's central record.
RN alone does not uniquely identify every child row.
Pipe, Date and Record help identify individual related records.
RN of Bore Replaced creates a logical self-reference between Registration records.
verificationChecks: Confirm the Oracle datatype, length and leading-zero behaviour.
Identify subject-table RNs missing from Registration.
Confirm physical foreign keys and indexes using Oracle metadata.
Determine how RNs are generated, allocated, reserved and retired.
Confirm whether RN of Bore Replaced is physically constrained.

lessons.title: Pipe, Date and Record
lessons.summary: Understand the additional identifiers used when a facility has multiple pipes or repeated records.
objectives: Understand the purpose of Date and Record.
lessons.contentMarkdown:
# Pipe, Date and Record

RN identifies the facility, but one facility can contain several pipes and many observations. GWDB therefore also uses **Pipe**, **Date** and **Record**.

- `A` represents a single pipe or the deepest pipe.
- `B`, `C` and later letters represent additional pipes.
- `X` represents a borehole before completion or material not directly related to a pipe.
- Date distinguishes observations over time.
- Record distinguishes repeated rows sharing other identifiers.

lessons.title: Registration Table
lessons.summary: Explore the central facility table, location fields, status, ownership and confidentiality.
lessons.contentMarkdown:
# Registration Table

Registration is the central facility table. It records identity, office, file references, facility type and status, geographic location, drilling information, map references, ownership, confidentiality, property and replacement relationships.

The data dictionary identifies Office, Facility Type and Facility Status as compulsory fields. Log Received Date cannot be before Drilled Date.

lessons.title: Construction and Casing
lessons.summary: Learn how casing and construction materials are recorded as depth intervals.
lessons.contentMarkdown:
# Construction and Casing

The Casing table stores materials associated with bore construction. A logical row is identified using RN, Pipe, Date and Record and includes material description, size, outside diameter, top and bottom depth.

Pipe `X` can be used for grout, gravel pack or other material not directly related to a completed pipe.

lessons.title: Strata, Aquifers and Lithology
lessons.summary: Understand geological intervals, water-bearing formations and lithology records.
lessons.contentMarkdown:
# Strata, Aquifers and Lithology

The Strata Log table describes geological layers using top depth, bottom depth and description. The Aquifer table records water-bearing intervals and related properties such as standing water level when drilled, flow, quality, yield, condition and formation.

The logical connection between Aquifer and Lithologies using RN and Record is inferred and must be verified from Oracle metadata.

lessons.title: Water Levels and Bore Logger Data
lessons.summary: Compare manual or derived water-level observations with logger-derived data.
objectives: Compare Water Level and Bore Logger Data.
lessons.contentMarkdown:
# Water Levels and Bore Logger Data

The Water Level table stores measurements from a recorded measuring point. Measurements are stored in metres. Values above the measurement point are positive and values below it are negative.

Bore Logger Data stores logger-derived observations and repeats much of the context used by Water Level. The lineage and deduplication behaviour must be confirmed from system processes.

lessons.title: Pumping Tests and Flow Readings
lessons.summary: Learn the pump-test header, test types and time-series reading structure.
lessons.contentMarkdown:
# Pumping Tests and Flow Readings

Pumping Test and Design records test setup and summary information. Pump Test Types records ordered test types. Flow and Pump Test Readings stores time, discharge, back pressure or drawdown, temperature and comments.

The likely header-detail relationship uses RN, Pipe, Date and Record, but the exact Oracle primary and foreign keys require schema verification.

lessons.title: Water Quality and Laboratory Analysis
lessons.summary: Understand field measurements, standard analyses and variable-based special analyses.
lessons.contentMarkdown:
# Water Quality and Laboratory Analysis

GWDB stores field measurements such as conductivity, pH, temperature and dissolved oxygen. The standard Water Analysis table uses fixed chemical columns. Special Water Analysis separates sample and bottle context from variable-based results.

Water Quality Variables defines names, units, limits, accuracy and precision for variable-based results.

lessons.title: Drillers, Notices and Drill Logs
lessons.summary: Explore driller licensing, notices, trainees and drill-log receivals.
objectives: Recognise RN linkage to drilling administration.
lessons.contentMarkdown:
# Drillers, Notices and Drill Logs

Driller records include licence, status, class, methods, restrictions, contact and office details. Drill Notices and Drill Log Receivals record drilling activities and workflow information. Driller Trainees links trainees to a driller licence context.

The physical relationships use licence identifiers and require Oracle constraint verification.

lessons.title: Oracle Forms, PL/SQL and Integrations
lessons.summary: Understand how the existing user interface, database programs, reporting and public-data channels fit together.
objectives: Recognise where business rules may be implemented.
lessons.contentMarkdown:
# Oracle Forms, PL/SQL and Integrations

The data dictionary describes an Oracle relational database running on Solaris and Oracle Forms running in a Microsoft Windows Server environment. District offices access the centrally located database through the departmental intranet.

Business rules may exist in Forms triggers, PL/SQL, database constraints and operational procedures. Schema, Forms source and integration access are required before those implementation details can be marked schema verified.
